_comment: Machine-readable twin of docs/model-fit.md. Per model: the operator characters it plays well, the ones it lacks, and the guidance a run should carry when ASSIST=fit. `measured` is regenerated by `scripts/model_fit.py update` from role_metrics over real sessions; `characters`/`guidance` are the human verdict and are edited by hand with a run to point at. Keys match the launcher's model short name (claude_relay_run.sh SHORT, local_relay_run.sh ALIAS).

guidance: You are fast and honest and you commit as you go — keep that. Your measured weakness is that on a wall you re-race the six-lane relay (9 relays, 0 single-lane probes, on both missions so far) and then attribute the symptom to the game ('trap warp', 'sealed') and stop. When two relay attempts end at the same tile, the next command is NOT a third relay: it is ONE lane, `uv run python scripts/agent.py rom/pokemon_red.gb --load-state <baton> --max-turns 300 --output-json probe.json`, with one hypothesis written down first.

Before you write 'unreachable' or 'sealed' about any map, state the furthest coordinate any lane actually stood on, from fitness.json. If that is near the edge you entered from, you have not explored the map; you have explored its doorway.
Keep working after the summary is written. Three of your runs ended with 80+ minutes left and an unsolved, named blocker; each was graded a failure of the run.
Your measured strength is the single-lane probe with one hypothesis each (9 probes to 1 relay on Brock). Keep the ratio; the relay is for confirming, not searching.
You are also the run most likely to catch an error in the mission or the staged seeds. When you do, write it into the learnings and keep going — do not work around it silently.

Your measured strength is reading and testing before racing (305 calls, 33 probes, five test files before one relay on Mt. Moon) — keep it. Your measured weakness is the verdict at the end: 'unreachable' from edges probed at x<=3 of a 70-tile map. Before any 'impossible' conclusion, state the furthest tile a lane stood on and whether the unexplored direction was walked at all.
You are slow per turn (19 s). Write each obstacle file the moment the obstacle is named, before the next relay call, so a compaction cannot lose it.
Budget: your long runs are your best runs. Do not end at 17 minutes; the 95-minute run reached Route 3.

Your cadence is the fastest on the box and your context discipline is the weakest: two runs ended in a compaction loop with no deliverable. Never read a file without an offset/limit or a grep; page through scripts/agent.py 150 lines at a time. After every relay call, write or update a docs/learnings file BEFORE doing anything else, and commit it. If you have read the same file twice, stop reading and act on what you have.
